scope: Proposition 5.19 (Bounded annular cap densities) of the manuscript “Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one” (preprints/Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bf15a86507a10184), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 63. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an ordinary square annulus of nonzero macroscopic width, with inner and outer rim sets A, E. There are C < ∞ and a mesh threshold depending only on q and this fixed geometry such that, below that threshold, every pair of separate noncrossing cap partitions X, Y on the two rims satisfies |IH(X, Y )| ≤ C. (5.45) The four pressures in H, H/X, H/Y, H/(X, Y ) between the rim images are uniformly bounded as well. The same conclusions hold for a fixed ordinary rectilinear polygonal annulus between two disjoint simple boundary cuts with positive separation. Constants may depend on this geometry; each rim must have a positive-length flat patch, and the ordinary bulk between the cuts must be connected. In particular a fixed thin ordinary polygonal collar with these properties is allowed. After attaching arbitrary planar graphs separately beyond the two cuts, changing an allowed cap on one side changes the opposite-side edge marginal by a uniformly bounded density and reciprocal density. This is a bounded comparison, not a density tending to one.
